description: We are passionate about AI, Data Science, and Software Development. We aim to build TerraTrend AI, a platform that analyzes NASA Earth data to detect environmental trends and visualize global changes. We welcome members skilled in Python, React, Machine Learning, Data Analysis, GIS, and UI/UX. We value creativity, teamwork, and problem-solving. Let's innovate for Earth! Also we new the full stack development.
summary:
TERRATREND AI is a full-stack environmental intelligence dashboard designed to decode the planet's changing systems. By integrating NASA POWER historical datasets with real-time Open-Meteo weather feeds and NOAA ocean temperatures, the platform allows users to investigate climate anomalies, identify sudden environmental shifts, and perform rigorous statistical trend analysis (using Mann-Kendall tests and Sen's Slope).
Addressing the challenge of accessible climate data, TERRATREND provides a dynamic "Live Vegetation Suitability" check and a Green/Yellow/Red environmental alert engine based on seasonal historical baselines. Users can explore spatial heatmaps, animate historical timelines, and generate automated AI-driven research summaries. The platform is built to be scientifically honest—every result includes data provenance, confidence scores, and explicit limitations, making complex Earth observation data accessible and actionable for researchers, policymakers, and the public.
details:
What does it do?
TERRATREND AI is a comprehensive web application that transforms raw Earth observation data into actionable environmental intelligence. Users can select specific geographical coordinates and analyze variables like temperature, precipitation, humidity, wind speed, and soil moisture. The platform features a live Vegetation Suitability index, real-time Sea Surface Temperature (NOAA), and a dynamic Alert System (Green/Yellow/Red) that compares live conditions against 10-year historical baselines.

How does it work?
The platform utilizes a React frontend and a Python FastAPI backend. It fetches historical data via the NASA POWER API and real-time weather via Open-Meteo. The backend performs rigorous statistical analysis using SciPy, Statsmodels, and PyMannKendall to calculate linear regression slopes, Sen's slopes, and Mann-Kendall trend significance. Machine learning techniques are simulated via a rule-based AI engine that generates scientific summaries, detects anomalies, and identifies sudden environmental shifts. The frontend visualizes this data using Recharts and React-Leaflet, rendering interactive time-series charts, spatial heatmaps, and animated "Time Machine" timelines.

Benefits and Impact:
The project democratizes access to complex climate data. By translating dense scientific metrics into intuitive UI elements—like confidence scores and live alert colors—it empowers policymakers, farmers, and researchers to make data-driven decisions. The "Live Vegetation Suitability" feature, for instance, provides immediate drought-stress insights, while the "Sudden Change Detector" helps identify rapid environmental degradation.

Tools and Technologies Used:

  • Frontend: React.js, Vite, Recharts, React-Leaflet, Lucide-React, Axios.
  • Backend: Python, FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pydantic.
  • Data Science: Pandas, NumPy, SciPy, Statsmodels, PyMannKendall.
  • External APIs: NASA POWER, Open-Meteo, NOAA Coral Reef Watch (ERDDAP).
  • Reporting: ReportLab (for PDF generation).

Creativity and Considerations:
The design prioritizes "Scientific Honesty." We intentionally included data provenance, missing-data warnings, and statistical caveats (e.g., distinguishing correlation from causation) directly in the UI. The custom Alert Engine does not rely on fixed thresholds; instead, it dynamically calculates seasonal Z-score anomalies based on the specific location's 10-year history. The dark-themed, glassmorphic UI is designed to feel like a futuristic mission control dashboard, making the exploration of climate data engaging and intuitive.
